title: Kinematics of Motion in a Straight Line Module 1 Lesson 2: Vertical Motion Gravity custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A particle is projected vertically upwards from ground level and reaches a greatest height of $45\text{ m}$ above the ground. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the initial speed of projection $u$ and the time taken to reach this greatest height.

A stone is thrown vertically downwards from the top of a cliff of height $50\text{ m}$ with an initial speed of $15\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and neglecting air resistance, calculate the speed with which the stone strikes the sea at the base of the cliff.

A ball is projected vertically upwards with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from a point $4\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the maximum height reached by the ball above the ground.

A particle is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the total time for which the particle is at a height of at least $40\text{ m}$ above the ground.

A stone is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with speed $26\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, find the velocity of the stone when it is at a height of $24\text{ m}$ above the ground on its downward path.

A particle is projected vertically upwards from the ground with speed $35\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The particle remains higher than $h\text{ m}$ above the ground for a continuous duration of $3\text{ s}$. Taking $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, calculate the value of $h$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with speed $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height reached by $P$ above the ground, and the time taken from projection to reach this maximum height.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the length of time for which $P$ is at a height of at least $19\text{ m}$ above the ground.

questions.prompt: A small ball is thrown vertically upwards with speed $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from a balcony that is $15\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground. The ball moves freely under gravity. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height reached by the ball above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the ball just before it strikes the ground, and the total time taken from the instant of throwing until it hits the ground.

questions.prompt: Particle $A$ is projected vertically upwards from ground level with speed $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Exactly $1\text{ s}$ later, a second particle $B$ is projected vertically upwards from the same point on the ground with speed $35\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Both particles move freely under gravity along parallel vertical lines. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the time $t$ elapsed from the instant particle $A$ is projected until the two particles are at the same height above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the height at which the two particles meet, and determine whether particle $A$ is rising or falling at this instant.

questions.prompt: A hot-air balloon is ascending vertically at a constant speed of $5\text{ m s}^{-1}$. When the balloon is at a height of $60\text{ m}$ above horizontal ground, a ballast bag is released from the balloon and moves freely under gravity. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum height above the ground reached by the ballast bag.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of the bag when it strikes the ground, and the time taken from the instant of release until the bag hits the ground.

questions.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest from the top of a vertical cliff. It takes $0.2\text{ s}$ to fall past a vertical window of height $2.2\text{ m}$ in a tower built against the cliff face. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the stone as it passes the top of the window.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the distance the stone fell from rest before reaching the top of the window, and find the speed of the stone as it leaves the bottom of the window.

questions.prompt: A vertical cliff of height $120\text{ m}$ stands on horizontal ground. At time $t = 0$, stone $A$ is dropped from rest from the top of the cliff. At the same instant, stone $B$ is projected vertically upwards from the base of the cliff with speed $U\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The two stones move along parallel vertical lines. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the two stones are at the same height above the ground at time $t = \frac{120}{U}$, and find the value of $U$ given that the stones pass each other at a height of $75\text{ m}$ above the ground.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using $U = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, find the speeds and directions of motion of both stones at the instant they pass each other, and find the maximum height reached by stone $B$.

questions.prompt: A particle $P$ is projected vertically upwards from a point $O$ on horizontal ground with initial speed $u\text{ m s}^{-1}$. It takes $1\text{ s}$ to reach point $A$, takes a further $1\text{ s}$ to travel from $A$ to point $B$ where $h_B - h_A = 25\text{ m}$, and takes a further $2\text{ s}$ to reach its highest point $C$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the speed of the particle as it passes point $B$ and determine its speed as it passes point $A$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the initial projection speed $u$ from the ground, and determine the heights $h_A$, $h_B$, and the maximum height $h_C$ above the ground.
